options.name: aws_sigv4
options.help: Use AWS V4 signature authentication in the transfer
options.heading: HTTP options
options.description:
Generate an `Authorization` header with an AWS SigV4 signature.

Use [`-u, --user`](#user) to specify Access Key Id (username) and Secret Key (password).

To use temporary session credentials (e.g. for an AWS IAM Role), add the `X-Amz-Security-Token` header containing the session token.

options.name: cacert_file
options.help: CA certificate to verify peer against (PEM format)
options.heading: HTTP options
options.description:
Specifies the certificate file for peer verification. The file may contain multiple CA certificates and must be in PEM format.
Normally Hurl is built to use a default file for this, so this option is typically used to alter that default file.

options.name: client_cert_file
options.help: Client certificate file and password
options.heading: HTTP options
options.description:
Client certificate file and password.

See also [`--key`](#key).

options.name: color
options.help: Colorize output
options.heading: Output options
options.description:
Colorize standard output and standard error.

By default, Hurl outputs a prettified and colorized response. When redirected through pipes, standard streams are not colorized and color can be forced with this option.

options.name: compressed
options.help: Request compressed response (using deflate or gzip)
options.heading: HTTP options
options.description: Request a compressed response using one of the algorithms br, gzip, deflate and automatically decompress the content.

options.name: connect_timeout
options.help: Maximum time allowed for connection
options.heading: HTTP options
options.description:
Maximum time in seconds that you allow Hurl's connection to take.

You can specify time units in the connect timeout expression. Set Hurl to use a connect timeout of 20 seconds with `--connect-timeout 20s` or set it to 35,000 milliseconds with `--connect-timeout 35000ms`. No spaces allowed.

See also [`-m, --max-time`](#max-time).

options.name: connect_to
options.help: For a request to the given HOST1:PORT1 pair, connect to HOST2:PORT2 instead
options.heading: HTTP options
options.description:
For a request to the given HOST1:PORT1 pair, connect to HOST2:PORT2 instead. This option can be used several times in a command line.

See also [`--resolve`](#resolve).

options.name: continue_on_error
options.help: Continue executing requests even if an error occurs
options.heading: Run options
options.description:
Continue executing requests to the end of the Hurl file even when an assert error occurs. By default, Hurl exits after an assert error in the HTTP response.

Note that this option does not affect the behavior with multiple input Hurl files.

All the input files are executed independently. The result of one file does not affect the execution of the other Hurl files.

options.name: cookies_input_file
options.help: Read cookies from FILE
options.heading: Other options
options.description:
Read cookies from FILE (using the Netscape cookie file format).

Combined with [`-c, --cookie-jar`](#cookie-jar), you can simulate a cookie storage between successive Hurl runs.

options.name: cookies_output_file
options.help: Write cookies to FILE after running the session
options.heading: Other options
options.description:
Write cookies to FILE after running the session.
The file will be written using the Netscape cookie file format.

Combined with [`-b, --cookie`](#cookie), you can simulate a cookie storage between successive Hurl runs.

options.name: curl
options.help: Export each request to a list of curl commands
options.heading: Output options
options.description: Export each request to a list of curl commands.

options.name: delay
options.help: Sets delay before each request (aka sleep)
options.heading: Run options
options.description:
Sets delay before each request (aka sleep). The delay is not applied to requests that have been retried because of [`--retry`](#retry). See [`--retry-interval`](#retry-interval) to space retried requests.

You can specify time units in the delay expression. Set Hurl to use a delay of 2 seconds with `--delay 2s` or set it to 500 milliseconds with `--delay 500ms`. Supported time units: ms, s, m, h. No spaces allowed.

options.name: digest
options.help: Tell Hurl to use HTTP Digest authentication
options.heading: HTTP options
options.description: Tell Hurl to use HTTP Digest authentication

options.name: error_format
options.help: Control the format of error messages
options.heading: Output options
options.description: Control the format of error message (short by default or long).  When using long, the response body is logged when there are errors.

options.name: fail_with_body
options.help: Output body response if there are any errors
options.heading: Output options
options.description: Output body response on standard output if there are any errors. By default, Hurl outputs the last body response on standard output only when a run is successful.

options.name: file_root
options.help: Set root directory to import files [default: input file directory]
options.heading: Other options
options.description:
Set root directory to import files in Hurl. This is used for files in multipart form data, request body and response output.
When it is not explicitly defined, files are relative to the Hurl file's directory.

options.name: from_entry
options.help: Execute Hurl file from ENTRY_NUMBER (starting at 1)
options.heading: Run options
options.description: Execute Hurl file from ENTRY_NUMBER (starting at 1).

options.name: glob
options.help: Specify input files that match the given GLOB. Multiple glob flags may be used
options.heading: Other options
options.description:
Specify input files that match the given glob pattern.

Multiple glob flags may be used. This flag supports common Unix glob patterns like *, ? and [].
However, to avoid your shell accidentally expanding glob patterns before Hurl handles them, you must use single quotes or double quotes around each pattern.

options.name: header
options.help: Pass custom header(s) to server
options.heading: HTTP options
options.description:
Add an extra header to include in information sent. Can be used several times in a command.

Do not add newlines or carriage returns.

options.name: http10
options.help: Tell Hurl to use HTTP version 1.0
options.heading: HTTP options
options.description: Tells Hurl to use HTTP version 1.0 instead of using its internally preferred HTTP version.

options.name: http11
options.help: Tell Hurl to use HTTP version 1.1
options.heading: HTTP options
options.description: Tells Hurl to use HTTP version 1.1.

options.name: http2
options.help: Tell Hurl to use HTTP version 2
options.heading: HTTP options
options.description:
Tells Hurl to use HTTP version 2.
For HTTPS, this means Hurl negotiates HTTP/2 in the TLS handshake. Hurl does this by default.
For HTTP, this means Hurl attempts to upgrade the request to HTTP/2 using the Upgrade: request header.

options.name: http2_prior_knowledge
options.help: Tell Hurl to use HTTP version 2 without HTTP/1.1 Upgrade
options.heading: HTTP options
options.description: Tells Hurl to issue a non-TLS HTTP request using HTTP/2 directly without HTTP/1.1 Upgrade. It requires prior knowledge that the server supports HTTP/2 straight away. HTTPS requests still do HTTP/2 the standard way with negotiated protocol versions in the TLS handshake.

options.name: http3
options.help: Tell Hurl to use HTTP version 3
options.heading: HTTP options
options.description: Tells Hurl to try HTTP version 3 to the host in the URL, but fallback to earlier HTTP versions if the HTTP/3 connection establishment fails. HTTP/3 is only available for HTTPS and not for HTTP URLs.

options.name: include
options.help: Include the HTTP headers in the output
options.heading: Output options
options.description: Include the HTTP headers in the output

options.name: insecure
options.help: Allow insecure SSL connections
options.heading: HTTP options
options.description: This option explicitly allows Hurl to perform "insecure" SSL connections and transfers.

options.name: ipv4
options.help: Tell Hurl to use IPv4 addresses only when resolving host names, and not for example try IPv6
options.heading: HTTP options
options.description: This option tells Hurl to use IPv4 addresses only when resolving host names, and not for example try IPv6.

options.name: ipv6
options.help: Tell Hurl to use IPv6 addresses only when resolving host names, and not for example try IPv4
options.heading: HTTP options
options.description: This option tells Hurl to use IPv6 addresses only when resolving host names, and not for example try IPv4.

options.name: jobs
options.help: Maximum number of parallel jobs, 1 to disable parallel execution
options.heading: Run options
options.description:
Maximum number of parallel jobs in parallel mode. Default value corresponds (in most cases) to the current amount of CPUs. Set to 1 to disable parallel execution of files.

See also [`--parallel`](#parallel).

options.name: json
options.help: Output each Hurl file result to JSON
options.heading: Output options
options.description: Output each Hurl file result to JSON. The format is very closed to HAR format.

options.name: client_key_file
options.help: Private key file name
options.heading: HTTP options
options.description: Private key file name.

options.name: limit_rate
options.help: Specify the maximum transfer rate in bytes/second, for both downloads and uploads
options.heading: HTTP options
options.description:
Specify the maximum transfer rate you want Hurl to use, for both downloads and uploads. This feature is useful if you have a limited pipe and you would like your transfer not to use your entire bandwidth. To make it slower than it otherwise would be.
The given speed is measured in bytes/second.

options.name: follow_location
options.help: Follow redirects
options.heading: HTTP options
options.description: Follow redirect. To limit the amount of redirects to follow use the [`--max-redirs`](#max-redirs) option

options.name: follow_location_trusted
options.help: Follow redirects but allows sending the name + password to all hosts that the site may redirect to
options.heading: HTTP options
options.description:
Like [`-L, --location`](#location), but allows sending the name + password to all hosts that the site may redirect to.
This may or may not introduce a security breach if the site redirects you to a site to which you send your authentication info (which is plaintext in the case of HTTP Basic authentication).

options.name: max_filesize
options.help: Specify the maximum size in bytes of a file to download
options.heading: HTTP options
options.description: Specify the maximum size in bytes of a file to download. If the file requested is larger than this value, the transfer does not start.

options.name: max_redirects
options.help: Maximum number of redirects allowed, -1 for unlimited redirects
options.heading: HTTP options
options.description:
Set maximum number of redirection-followings allowed

By default, the limit is set to 50 redirections. Set this option to -1 to make it unlimited.

options.name: max_time
options.help: Maximum time allowed for the transfer
options.heading: HTTP options
options.description:
Maximum time in seconds that you allow a request/response to take. This is the standard timeout.

You can specify time units in the maximum time expression. Set Hurl to use a maximum time of 20 seconds with `--max-time 20s` or set it to 35,000 milliseconds with `--max-time 35000ms`. No spaces allowed.

See also [`--connect-timeout`](#connect-timeout).

options.name: negotiate
options.help: Tell Hurl to use Negotiate (SPNEGO) authentication
options.heading: HTTP options
options.description: Tell Hurl to use Negotiate (SPNEGO) authentication.

options.name: netrc
options.help: Must read .netrc for username and password
options.heading: Other options
options.description:
Scan the .netrc file in the user's home directory for the username and password.

See also [`--netrc-file`](#netrc-file) and [`--netrc-optional`](#netrc-optional).

options.name: netrc_file
options.help: Specify FILE for .netrc
options.heading: Other options
options.description:
Like [`--netrc`](#netrc), but provide the path to the netrc file.

See also [`--netrc-optional`](#netrc-optional).

options.name: netrc_optional
options.help: Use either .netrc or the URL
options.heading: Other options
options.description:
Similar to [`--netrc`](#netrc), but make the .netrc usage optional.

See also [`--netrc-file`](#netrc-file).

options.name: no_assert
options.help: Ignore asserts defined in the Hurl file
options.heading: Run options
options.description: Ignore all asserts defined in the Hurl file.

options.name: no_color
options.help: Do not colorize output
options.heading: Output options
options.description: Do not colorize standard output nor standard error.

options.name: no_cookie_store
options.help: Do not use cookie store between requests
options.heading: HTTP options
options.description: Do not use cookie storage for requests/responses in a file. By default, requests in the same Hurl file share cookie storage, this option deactivates cookie engine.

options.name: no_header
options.help: Remove header(s) sent to server
options.heading: HTTP options
options.description: Remove a header from information sent. Can be used several times in a command.

options.name: no_jsonpath_coercion
options.help: Disable JSONPath result coercion
options.heading: Run options
options.description:
Disable JSONPath result coercion.

By default, when JSONPath coercion is enabled, empty JSONPath results are returned as no value and single JSONPath results are returned as a scalar value. With this option, JSONPath results are always returned as arrays.

options.name: no_output
options.help: Suppress output. By default, Hurl outputs the body of the last response
options.heading: Output options
options.description: Suppress output. By default, Hurl outputs the body of the last response.

options.name: no_pretty
options.help: Do not prettify response output
options.heading: Output options
options.description:
Do not prettify response output for supported content type (JSON only for the moment). By default, output is prettified if
standard output is a terminal.

options.name: no_proxy
options.help: List of hosts which do not use proxy
options.heading: HTTP options
options.description: Comma-separated list of hosts which do not use a proxy.

options.name: ntlm
options.help: Tell Hurl to use NTLM authentication
options.heading: HTTP options
options.description: Tell Hurl to use NTLM authentication

options.name: output
options.help: Write to FILE instead of stdout
options.heading: Output options
options.description: Write output to FILE instead of stdout. Use '-' for stdout in [Options] sections.

options.name: parallel
options.help: Run files in parallel (default in test mode)
options.heading: Run options
options.description:
Run files in parallel.

Each Hurl file is executed in its own worker thread, without sharing anything with the other workers. The default run mode is sequential. Parallel execution is by default in [`--test`](#test) mode.

See also [`--jobs`](#jobs).

options.name: path_as_is
options.help: Tell Hurl to not handle sequences of /../ or /./ in the given URL path
options.heading: HTTP options
options.description: Tell Hurl to not handle sequences of /../ or /./ in the given URL path. Normally Hurl will squash or merge them according to standards but with this option set you tell it not to do that.

options.name: pinned_pub_key
options.help: Public key to verify peer against
options.heading: HTTP options
options.description: When negotiating a TLS or SSL connection, the server sends a certificate indicating its identity. A public key is extracted from this certificate and if it does not exactly match the public key provided to this option, Hurl aborts the connection before sending or receiving any data.

options.name: pretty
options.help: Prettify JSON response output
options.heading: Output options
options.description: Prettify response output for supported content type (JSON only for the moment). By default, JSON response is prettified if standard output is a terminal, and colorized, see[`--no-color`](#no-color) to format without color.

options.name: progress_bar
options.help: Display a progress bar in test mode
options.heading: Output options
options.description: Display a progress bar in test mode. The progress bar is displayed only in interactive TTYs. This option forces the progress bar to be displayed even in non-interactive TTYs.

options.name: proxy
options.help: Use proxy on given PROTOCOL/HOST/PORT
options.heading: HTTP options
options.description: Use the specified proxy.

options.name: proxy_header
options.help: Extra header to include in the request when sending to a proxy
options.heading: HTTP options
options.description: Extra header to include in the request when sending to a proxy. These headers are only applied when a proxy is involved; if Hurl connects directly to the target server, they are ignored.

options.name: repeat
options.help: Repeat the input files sequence NUM times, -1 for infinite loop
options.heading: Run options
options.description:
Repeat the input files sequence NUM times, -1 for infinite loop. Given a.hurl, b.hurl, c.hurl as input, repeat two
times will run a.hurl, b.hurl, c.hurl, a.hurl, b.hurl, c.hurl.

options.name: report_html
options.help: Generate HTML report to DIR
options.heading: Report options
options.description:
Generate HTML report in DIR.

If the HTML report already exists, it will be updated with the new test results.

options.name: report_json
options.help: Generate JSON report to DIR
options.heading: Report options
options.description:
Generate JSON report in DIR.

If the JSON report already exists, it will be updated with the new test results.

options.name: report_junit
options.help: Write a JUnit XML report to FILE
options.heading: Report options
options.description:
Generate JUnit File.

If the FILE report already exists, it will be updated with the new test results.

options.name: report_tap
options.help: Write a TAP report to FILE
options.heading: Report options
options.description:
Generate TAP report.

If the FILE report already exists, it will be updated with the new test results.

options.name: resolve
options.help: Provide a custom address for a specific HOST and PORT pair
options.heading: HTTP options
options.description: Provide a custom address for a specific host and port pair. Using this, you can make the Hurl requests(s) use a specified address and prevent the otherwise normally resolved address to be used. Consider it a sort of /etc/hosts alternative provided on the command line.

options.name: retry
options.help: Maximum number of retries, 0 for no retries, -1 for unlimited retries
options.heading: Run options
options.description: Maximum number of retries, 0 for no retries, -1 for unlimited retries. Retry happens if any error occurs (asserts, captures, runtimes etc...).

options.name: retry_interval
options.help: Interval in milliseconds before a retry
options.heading: Run options
options.description:
Duration in milliseconds between each retry. Default is 1000 ms.

You can specify time units in the retry interval expression. Set Hurl to use a retry interval of 2 seconds with `--retry-interval 2s` or set it to 500 milliseconds with `--retry-interval 500ms`. No spaces allowed.

options.name: secret
options.help: Define a variable which value is secret
options.heading: Run options
options.description: Define secret value to be redacted from logs and report. When defined, secrets can be used as variable everywhere variables are used.

options.name: secrets_file
options.help: Define a secrets file in which you define your secrets
options.heading: Run options
options.description:
Define a secrets file in which you define your secrets

Each secret is defined as name=value exactly as with [`--secret`](#secret) option.

Note that defining a secret twice produces an error.

options.name: ssl_no_revoke
options.help: (Windows) Tell Hurl to disable certificate revocation checks
options.heading: HTTP options
options.description: (Windows) This option tells Hurl to disable certificate revocation checks. WARNING: this option loosens the SSL security, and by using this flag you ask for exactly that.

options.name: test
options.help: Activate test mode (use parallel execution)
options.heading: Run options
options.description:
Activate test mode: with this, the HTTP response is not outputted anymore, progress is reported for each Hurl file tested, and a text summary is displayed when all files have been run.

In test mode, files are executed in parallel. To run test in a sequential way use `--jobs 1`.

See also [`--jobs`](#jobs).

options.name: tls_max
options.help: Set the maximum allowed TLS version
options.heading: HTTP options
options.description:
Set the maximum allowed TLS version. If the connection is done without TLS, this option has no effect. This includes QUIC-using (HTTP/3) transfers.

default   Use up to the recommended TLS version.
1.0       Use up to TLSv1.0.
1.1       Use up to TLSv1.1.
1.2       Use up to TLSv1.2.
1.3       Use up to TLSv1.3.

options.name: tls_min
options.help: Set the minimum allowed TLS version
options.heading: HTTP options
options.description:
Set the minimum allowed TLS version. If the connection is done without TLS, this option has no effect. This includes QUIC-using (HTTP/3) transfers.

default   Use down to the recommended TLS version.
1.0       Use down to TLSv1.0.
1.1       Use down to TLSv1.1.
1.2       Use down to TLSv1.2.
1.3       Use down to TLSv1.3.

options.name: to_entry
options.help: Execute Hurl file to ENTRY_NUMBER (starting at 1)
options.heading: Run options
options.description:
Execute Hurl file to ENTRY_NUMBER (starting at 1).
Ignore the remaining of the file. It is useful for debugging a session.

options.name: unix_socket
options.help: (HTTP) Connect through this Unix domain socket, instead of using the network
options.heading: HTTP options
options.description: (HTTP) Connect through this Unix domain socket, instead of using the network.

options.name: user
options.help: Add basic Authentication header to each request
options.heading: HTTP options
options.description: Add basic Authentication header to each request.

options.name: user_agent
options.help: Specify the User-Agent string to send to the HTTP server
options.heading: HTTP options
options.description: Specify the User-Agent string to send to the HTTP server.

options.name: variable
options.help: Define a variable
options.heading: Run options
options.description: Define variable (name/value) to be used in Hurl templates.

options.name: variables_file
options.help: Define a properties file in which you define your variables
options.heading: Run options
options.description:
Set properties file in which your define your variables.

Each variable is defined as name=value exactly as with [`--variable`](#variable) option.

Note that defining a variable twice produces an error.

options.name: verbose
options.help: Turn on verbose (alias to --verbosity verbose)
options.heading: Output options
options.description:
Turn on verbose output on standard error stream.
Useful for debugging.

A line starting with '>' means data sent by Hurl.
A line staring with '<' means data received by Hurl.
A line starting with '*' means additional info provided by Hurl.

If you only want HTTP headers in the output, [`-i, --include`](#include) might be the option you're looking for.

options.name: verbosity
options.help: Set verbosity level for debug log
options.heading: Output options
options.description:
Set the verbosity level for debug logs on standard error stream (brief, verbose or debug)

If you only want HTTP headers in the output, [`-i, --include`](#include) might be the option you're looking for.
[`-v, --verbose`](#verbose) is an alias for `--verbosity verbose`
[`--very-verbose`](#very-verbose) is an alias for `--verbosity debug`

options.name: very_verbose
options.help: Turn on very verbose output, including HTTP response and libcurl logs (alias to --verbosity debug)
options.heading: Output options
options.description:
Turn on more verbose output on standard error stream.

In contrast to  [`--verbose`](#verbose) option, this option outputs the full HTTP body request and response on standard error. In addition, lines starting with '**' are libcurl debug logs.
